title: "Forbidden Archaeology" Coauthor Michael Cremo Dead at 78
excerpt: ​ Forbidden Archaeology co-author Michael Cremo died this past week at the age of 78, according to the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKON), of which Cremo was a longtime member....
content:
​Forbidden Archaeology co-author Michael Cremo died this past week at the age of 78, according to the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKON), of which Cremo was a longtime member. The society reported that Cremo died sometime before October 11, when they posted his obituary. (Other sources give his date of death as October 14, but he had already been reported dead three days earlier.) Cremo gained fame in the “alternative archaeology” movement in 1993, when he and coauthor Richard Thompson published a doorstop 900-page volume, Forbidden Archaeology: The Hidden History of the Human Race, that used an academic tone to present erroneous, outdated, and sometimes fraudulent nineteenth century archaeological claims as evidence that humanity existed in its modern form for 40 million years. The book, and various abridgements and sequels, sold more than 300,000 copies.

​Born in 1948 in Schenectady, New York, to a miliary intelligence officer, Cremo became a counterculture enthusiast in the late 1960s, through which he developed an interest in Eastern philosophy. He joined ISKON in 1973, where he was known as Drutakarma Prabhu. He advocated Hindu creationism for most of his literary career, making him a unique Hindu voice in the American creationist movement. After initial fame as an author in the 1990s, he served as a talking head on cable TV shows like Ancient Aliens in the 2010s, and he gave a presentation on his fringe claims to Google employees in 2015.

 While Cremo’s books have served as research sources for later alternative archaeology writers, Cremo himself largely faded from the fringe history scene a decade ago. According to IMDB, his last media project was a film version of Forbidden Archaeology, completed in 2015; however, GAIA TV lists him as a talking head in several of its streaming series, including the first season of Ancient Civilizations, which ran in 2017.
